newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says CAP reform needed before enlargement.
newsitem.headline: EU says CAP reform needed before enlargement.

text.p: The European Commission estimates that further reforms of the European Union's common agricultural policy will be needed to prepare the bloc for expansion to eastern Europe.

"In view of the challenges...the Commission considers it indispensable to proceed with further reforms of the CAP," a draft document assessing the effect on EU agricultural policy of the EU's enlargement plans says.

The document, obtained by Reuters, said the reforms would improve the competitiveness of EU agriculture, allow it to participate in the expansion of world markets, prepare it for the next world trade liberalisation round and for the EU's eastward enlargement.

Among the measures expected to be proposed by the Commission in Strasbourg next Tuesday are fixing the cereals intervention price at a safety net level of 95.35 Ecus per tonne (from 119.19 Ecus) from the year 2000.
A non-crop-specific area payment would be set at 68 Ecus per tonne and the reference rate for compulsory land set-aside would be fixed at zero percent.

According to the document silage cereals, mainly silage maize, would be excluded from the regime. For protein crops an extra aid would be set at 13 Ecus per tonne to preserve their competitiveness with cereals and current supplements would be kept for durum wheat.
